history.period: Ancient (claimed Vedic/Puranic roots; present structure rebuilt after destruction)
history.summary: Major Tantric Shakti Peeth at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi (Bhera) rivers, enshrining the headless goddess Chhinnamastika, one of the ten Mahavidyas, shown holding her severed head and standing on Kamdev and Rati. The site is named as a Shakti Peeth in the Vedas/Puranas (claimed; unverified) and its Tantric-style architecture with dome-shaped apexes is compared to Assam's Kamrup temples. The ancient temple was destroyed and a new temple built retaining the original idol. Animal sacrifice is still practised on Tuesdays, Saturdays and during Kali Puja. The shrine has 'Dham' status because Rudra Mahadev guards it on all four sides: Kaleshwar (east, seq 1642), Narahna (west), Muchhkund (north), Shiv Bari (south). Tribal (Santal/Magru) traditions also worship here during Sharad Navratri. Devotional claims of 6,000+ year antiquity are legendary (unverified). Coordinates approximate (Rajrappa Project area).

name: Chhinnamasta Temple (Chinnamastika Mandir)
town_description: Rajrappa is a pilgrim town in Chitarpur block of Ramgarh district, at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi rivers. It is famous as the seat of the Chinnamastika Shakti Peeth, drawing thousands of pilgrims daily, and also hosts the Rajrappa coal mining project. The town has guesthouses, dharamshalas and local transport links from Ramgarh and Ranchi.
